expectations.text: Keeps equipment advice brief and secondary (audio first if mentioned)
expectations.evidence: Gear is clearly secondary. Section 1 refuses 'Spending first' because 'Gear doesn't decide whether this works.' Section 11 comes near the end, opens with 'Gear is the smallest part of this,' and sets the spend order as 'audio, stability, then camera, then overlays.' A USB dynamic mic or headset is the first item to buy, and a 'Don't buy yet' list defers the rest. It falls short of brief: section 11 still runs to Buy, Optional, Free and Don't-buy lists plus a four-scene overlay breakdown, which is fuller than a brief secondary mention needs.

expectations.text: Keeps equipment advice brief and secondary (audio first if mentioned)
expectations.evidence: Audio comes first: the microphone is the first row of the table, with the note 'Audio matters more than video', and the 'Lean total' line puts audio ahead of lights. But the advice is neither brief nor secondary. The Recommendation opens with 'Spend about $300–450 now'. Section 1, 'What to buy', is the first section: a 7-row table with brands, prices and notes, a lean/comfortable total, and 3 more setup bullets.
